label: F-02
title: The invariant trip-wire CLAUDE.md nominates for 'never expose a burn' is a four-name denylist, not an invariant check
fingerprintNote: sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass)[:16] - legacy form, empty entryPoint. Carried verbatim from sanitized.json; reproduces from fingerprintBasis.

classification.assetImpact: None directly. The project's nominated trip-wire for its own stated invariant ('Antimatter must never expose a burn outside a completed annihilation') is a four-name denylist rather than a property check, so it would not catch a new burn entry point under any name outside that list - including the H-01 path, which violates the invariant from the grantor's ledger while passing the test.
attackPath: 1. CLAUDE.md nominates test_noPublicBurnEntryPoints as the guard for the no-burn invariant.
2. The test probes four hard-coded names (:344-345).
3. Any future burn-exposing function under a different name, or any existing path that is economically a burn, passes silently.
classification.likelihood: N/A - it is a coverage defect, already demonstrated: H-01's invariant violation coexists with a passing test.

justification: Spec-conformance F-02 at Low: the stated invariant is not actually enforced by the artifact the project designates to enforce it. Reported in spec-conformance rather than QA because it is a faithfulness gap in the project's own control, and because a passing test is exactly the kind of false assurance that lets a real defect through - as H-01 shows it already has. No asset impact of its own, hence Low. The Tier-3 harness at workspace/antimatter/test/audit/invariant/ is a ready template for a real property assertion; note that harness is AUDIT-AUTHORED and must never be cited as project coverage or filed as a project file.
recommendation: Replace the name-denylist with a property assertion (totalSupply is non-decreasing across every non-annihilateFrom external call, exercised by fuzzed calldata) or a source assertion (a single _burn occurrence, inside annihilateFrom). The Tier-3 harness at workspace/antimatter/test/audit/invariant/ is a ready template.

sanitizer.reason: No known-issues document exists for this project (knownIssuesFile/Source null, knownIssues empty, verified at HEAD) so KI suppression has no authority; no C4 known-invalid class genuinely applies; not a malicious-owner vector; ledger empty so no prior entry to reconcile against.

additionalContext.specText: 'no new entry point that reaches _burn except annihilateFrom' ... 'test_noPublicBurnEntryPoints in test/Annihilation.t.sol is a trip-wire for this rule.' (lib/antimatter/CLAUDE.md)
additionalContext.deviation: The test asserts that four hardcoded selectors revert: burn(uint256), burn(address,uint256), burnFrom(address,uint256), annihilate(address,uint256). It cannot detect what the rule prohibits - ANY new entry point reaching _burn - because a burn path under any other name is simply not in the list and the test passes green. Two further gaps: the rule also names 'no transfer to address(0) path' and 'no owner-callable clawback', and neither is probed at all (transfer-to-zero happens to be closed by OpenZeppelin's _update, i.e. by the base class, not by anything this repo asserts).
additionalContext.encodingDefect: All four signatures are encoded with two arguments (abi.encodeWithSignature(signatures[i], user, 1 ether)), so the one-argument burn(uint256) probe passes trailing calldata the decoder ignores - it would decode amount = uint256(uint160(user)) = 2827 wei rather than 1 ether. It would still catch a naive burn(uint256), but only because the address literal happens to be a small non-zero number. The probe is not testing what it reads as testing.
additionalContext.invariantHoldsAt0bb82d8: YES. src/Antimatter.sol contains exactly one _burn (:215, inside annihilateFrom) and one _mint (:180, onlyApprovedMinters). No ERC20Burnable inheritance, no burn/burnFrom/clawback, transfer-to-zero blocked by OZ v5.6.1 _update. Tier-3 invariant_08 independently proves it dynamically: an exact equality (totalSupply == sum minted - sum burned-in-completed-annihilation) over 76,800 calls per campaign on both Foundry and Medusa, with ~3,000 annihilations reverting AFTER reaching _burn and not one unaccounted unit.
additionalContext.note: Guard-quality finding. CLAUDE.md designates this test as the enforcement mechanism for a load-bearing invariant and instructs future authors not to weaken it, so false assurance here is the whole harm.

mergeAction: Kept as its own entry. Related to DEDUP-001 (whose exploit the trip-wire also fails to catch) but a distinct root cause: guard quality, not a live burn exposure. The invariant_08 PASS is folded in as evidence, not as a separate finding.
